coverageSpotVerification.detail: M8 is adjudicated capability-failure on two categorically non-exercising mappings. m8-a06 ('an older heavily-liked post (>24h) is absent from Trending') maps to a case that creates three posts seconds earlier and asserts that two RECENT posts are PRESENT - no post older than 24h exists anywhere in it, and dropping the 24-hour filter would make the mapped test MORE likely to pass. m8-a07 ('a like-count tie breaks newest-first') maps to a case in which the three posts hold 2, 1 and 0 likes - no tie is ever constructed and no ordering beyond the top item is asserted. I verified independently that the product satisfies both (see trace.md §4.8); the adjudication is about the coverage claim, not the feature. Weak-but-not-adjudicated mappings recorded for the record: m1-a10 (mapped case performs no upload; the seed's profile-set replay does, through the app's write path), m1-a11 (asserts a non-null avatarUrl string, not a render), m2-a12/m2-a13 (source greps of linkify.tsx and app/index.tsx rather than runtime observation; the negative no-unfurl form is defensible, the positive one is not), m3-a11 (source grep whose 'msg-' disjunct is near-vacuous, though the referenced code genuinely implements the jump), m2-a22 (asserts items.length <= 20, vacuous, and fetches page 2 only conditionally), m2-a24 (checks duplicates on the Global tab only and never checks gaps). Each of those either points at real implementing code or transitively exercises the observable, and each was independently verified in phase 3, so none is adjudicated. Structural note: most suite cases call service.* in process rather than through the HTTP API - inside the rules, but it means no suite-required assertion with a UI clause is ever observed by the suite.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ('core features partially work; several checklist items fail') and the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap'), placed nearer 30. Denominator rule applied: every milestone of the run's full scope counts, and non-green milestones score their checklists not passed; M8, adjudicated capability-failure on a dishonest coverage mapping, scores its checklist not passed.
O1.justification: Of the 101 M1-M7 assertions listed in assertions.json 0.3.0-m8 and keyed here, 56 pass, 17 fail and 28 are not-run; adding M8's 18 assertions as not-passed per the capability-failure rule gives 56 of 119, about 47% of the full-scope checklist. Only M1 is green (its choreography segment summary records green:true). M2's choreography ended early with 2 of 3 recorded checks failed and no segment summary; M3's segment summary records green:false / choreography-failed with 0 of 6 required checks passing; M4, M5, M6 and M8 have no choreography receipts at all; M7 was never attempted (no m7 runner, no receipt); the scale replay aborted before replaying an action. The brief's per-milestone platform proof is also absent everywhere - artifacts/ios-hermes/ is empty and every iOS Hermes export failed on hermesc. That is well short of 'M1-M4 solid': M3, the messaging core of a messenger, has an unusable conversation screen in the web build. It is clearly above the 30 anchor, though: M1 is fully green, the M2/M4/M5/M6 service-layer suites pass in my own clean run, and the M4/M5 grader-class window, revocation and ephemerality assertions all pass under the shortened-windows config.

O2.anchorsCited: At or slightly below the 30 anchor ('multiple high-severity defects in core flows'); far from the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path').
O2.justification: Four blocker-class defects, three of them in core flows and one an outright authorization break: d-01, GET /conversations/:id hands a non-member the member roster and the last message body of a private DM; d-02, GET /internal/push-log is unauthenticated and returns every user's push payloads including message previews; d-04, the conversation screen crashes on load in the web build (reproduced in three independent sessions); d-05, GET /profiles/:handle 500s for an active author with no concurrent load, on 3 of 3 sequential attempts. Five more major defects follow: d-03 unauthenticated digest trigger, d-06 the write-idempotency ruling violated for every toggle operation, d-07 1 Hz polling that defeats pagination and saturates the pool, d-08 duplicate contract test IDs bound to no-op buttons in a z-index:9999 overlay, d-09 auth-provider flakiness surfaced as 401 and logging users out. Placed below 30 rather than at it because d-01 is a direct read of another user's private message content, which the rubric treats as the worst class of finding. Held above the floor because the checks a probe set would go after first are largely right: history, sending, typing, member management and search are all membership- and role-scoped; window enforcement is server-side against server time and ignores caller-supplied timestamps; view-once media is never handed out as a fetchable path; deleted media 404s; expired content is filtered from history, search and digest counts.

O5.bandRationale: First-match branch 0: 'invariant manifest does not conform (including a named-fixture mismatch) OR replay's wall cap was exhausted'. The replay was attempted - artifacts/scale-replay.log records 'scale-replay start=1788652491 tenant=scale' and 'starter seeded on scale tenant' - so O5 is applicable and cannot be null. It then aborted inside applySchema with '(EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max clients are limited to pool_size: 15' (server/db.mjs:46 via scripts/scale-replay.mjs:18), before a single scale-log action replayed. Consequently artifacts/scale-replay.json (the script's own counts-vs-manifest report) does not exist, no 10%/50% checkpoint records exist anywhere in the lane, and there are no probe samples, p95 figures or named-fixture checks (celebrity follower count, the probe user's 500 follows, the busy group's 50-member roster). A replay that never built the corpus cannot conform to fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json, and the brief is explicit that any manifest nonconformance caps O5 at its failure band: 'performance is never scored on an artifact that did not validly reach the envelope, nor against an underfilled workload.' Branch 0 fires before branches 30/60/90/75 are considered.

notes: N=1 calibration grading, not a claim-eligible wave. Three recorded deviations from the frozen grader prompt, directed by the wave wrapper. (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped: wave.probeSetSha256 records the literal string 'none-uncommitted' and probeResults is empty. No probes were invented. O3 is scored only from the wave's rotated holdout probes, so it would have had no scoring input regardless; as it happens O3 is null on its own applicability predicate as well. (2) The grading family has not passed the calibration gate, so grader.calibrationPassed is false; sameFamilyGraded is false (the builder is a Grok lane, the grader is claude/claude-opus-5). The record labels this grade uncalibrated-grader. (3) Timing-sensitive checks are best-of-3 as the prompt requires, and host load is recorded beside them: uptime 1-minute load averages ranged 10.12 to 28.83 across the session because other sessions share this machine. SCHEMA LIMITATION: this report schema is version 1 and its assertionResults patternProperties only admits ^m[1-7]-a[0-9]{2}$, so M8's 18 assertions (added by LLP 0201's 2026-08-11 amendment, present in assertions.json 0.3.0-m8) cannot be keyed here. They were executed in full and are recorded in trace.md §4.8, and M8 is counted in O1's denominator as not-passed per the capability-failure adjudication in coverageSpotVerification. LANE RECORD: the lane wrote no run-record.json, so milestone statuses were derived from receipts/*-suite.json, receipts/*-choreo.jsonl, receipts/suite-status.json and receipts/simulator-status.json plus my own execution. Milestone statuses as I read them: M1 green; M2, M3, M4, M5, M6 attempted but not green; M7 not-run; M8 attempted and adjudicated capability-failure; scale replay attempted and aborted. M6 is not green (no choreography receipt, no segment summary, no simulator artifact), which is why O3 and O4 are null under applicability.json's m6-green predicates. HONESTY CREDIT: receipts/simulator-status.json records both simulator proofs as pass:false with the reason 'iOS Hermes bundle export failed ...; simulator proof not run; not faked', which is exactly the honest negative the instrument asks for.
